description: A two-panel composite TEM figure for a 29Mn-9.6Al-0.56C (wt.%) low-density steel; each panel pairs a selected-area diffraction pattern with a dark-field micrograph, and the panels are stacked out of alphabetical order — (b) occupies the upper half and (a) the lower half. Both diffraction patterns are labelled [011]α and indexed with the 000, 0–22, 1̄11, 2̄00 and 400 reflections; the {111} superlattice and {200} reflections whose relative intensity distinguishes B2 from DO3 order are present in both. (a) is the as-quenched sample: its dark-field image, formed with the {200} reflection (per caption), is a nearly featureless, finely speckled field in which no individual ordered domains can be resolved. (b) is the same alloy after 1 h of aging at 550 °C: with the same dark-field reflection the image resolves bright, equiaxed ordered domains a few tens of nanometres across, separated by dark boundaries. Both dark-field images carry a 100 nm scale bar. The figure demonstrates that ferrite of the as-quenched alloy is already partly ordered and that aging at 550 °C coarsens the ordering into a well-developed domain structure.

subfigures.description: As-quenched sample: SAED pattern along [011]α with indexed 000, 0–22, 1̄11, 2̄00 and 400 spots (superlattice reflections present), above a dark-field image taken with the {200} reflection that appears as a uniform, finely speckled field with no resolvable ordered domains. 100 nm scale bar at bottom left.

After 1 h of aging at 550 °C: SAED pattern along the same [011]α zone axis with the same indexed spots, above a dark-field image taken with the {200} reflection showing distinct bright equiaxed ordered domains (tens of nanometres) separated by dark boundaries. 100 nm scale bar at bottom left.

observations.observation: The group is composite: each panel contains a SAED pattern (upper) and a dark-field TEM micrograph (lower), and the two halves belong to two different heat-treatment states of the same alloy.
Both diffraction patterns are labelled [011]α and are indexed with the same spot set: 000, 0–22, 1̄11, 2̄00 and 400.

In panel (a) the {111}-type spot appears clearly weaker than the {200}-type spot, whereas in panel (b) the two are of comparable brightness; the pixel evidence is qualitative only because no intensity scale is given.

The dark-field micrograph of (a) is a nearly uniform speckled field with no resolvable domain contrast, while that of (b) shows bright equiaxed domains of a few tens of nanometres separated by dark boundaries.
Both dark-field micrographs carry a 100 nm scale bar printed in the lower-left corner.
Panel (b) is placed above panel (a) in the figure layout, so reading order and panel lettering are inverted.
The caption states that the dark-field images were recorded using the {200} reflection and that the diffraction patterns are of ferrite in the [011] zone axis.
The caption identifies (a) as the as-quenched sample and (b) as the sample after 1 h of aging at 550 °C, for a 29Mn-9.6Al-0.56C (wt.%) alloy.
The citing text states the alloy was first treated at 850 °C for 10 min, water quenched and then aged at 550 °C for 1 h.

The citing text states that the extra spots in the as-quenched ferrite pattern correspond to ordered structures, {111} indicating DO3 and {200} being consistent with either DO3 or B2, and that the intensity difference between them shows the initial ferrite is a mixture of B2 and another ordered state.

The citing text states that after aging at 550 °C (Fig. 9b) there is no longer an intensity difference between the {111} and {200} reflections, i.e. ferrite becomes fully ordered DO3 — this interpretation is not quantitatively verifiable from the pixels alone.
The citing text describes the ferrite orientation as the [110] zone axis, while the figure and its caption label it [011]α; these are the same zone axis written in different notation.

measured_quantities: ordered-domain size (nm, from the 100 nm scale bar)
unreadable_items: No intensity scale or exposure calibration is printed on either diffraction pattern, so spot-intensity differences (the B2/DO3 diagnostic) can only be judged qualitatively
No numeric domain size is annotated in panel (b); sizes can only be estimated against the 100 nm scale bar
The caption does not state which ordered phase the {200} dark-field reflection itself belongs to in each state
